vehicles.name: Toyota Prius (Red)

vehicles.name: Toyota KDH Van
vehicles.description: Spacious air-conditioned KDH van with plenty of luggage room, ideal for families and small groups.

destinations.name: Negombo
destinations.description: A relaxed fishing town and beach resort right next to the airport, with a lively fish market, old Dutch fort and canals. The ideal first or last night.

destinations.name: Colombo
destinations.description: Sri Lanka's commercial capital: colonial architecture, Galle Face Green at sunset, Pettah markets, museums and a fast-growing food scene.

destinations.name: Sigiriya
destinations.description: The 5th-century Lion Rock fortress rising 200 m above the jungle, with ancient frescoes, a mirror wall and sweeping views from the summit.
destinations.bestTime: January to April, July to September

destinations.name: Dambulla
destinations.description: A UNESCO-listed cave temple complex with five caves holding more than 150 Buddha statues and vivid ceiling paintings.
destinations.bestTime: January to April, July to September

destinations.name: Polonnaruwa
destinations.description: The medieval capital with beautifully preserved ruins, the Gal Vihara rock carvings and lakeside cycling routes.

destinations.name: Kandy
destinations.description: The last royal capital set around a lake, home to the Temple of the Tooth, cultural dance shows and botanical gardens.

destinations.name: Nuwara Eliya
destinations.description: Little England among rolling tea estates, waterfalls and cool mountain air. Visit a tea factory and Horton Plains nearby.

destinations.name: Ella
destinations.description: A laid-back mountain village known for the Nine Arches Bridge, Little Adam's Peak and one of the world's most scenic train rides.

destinations.name: Udawalawe
destinations.description: A compact national park where herds of wild elephants are almost guaranteed on a morning or afternoon jeep safari.

destinations.name: Yala National Park
destinations.description: Sri Lanka's most famous wildlife park with one of the world's highest densities of leopards, plus elephants, sloth bears and birds.

destinations.name: Galle
destinations.description: A UNESCO-listed Dutch fort town of cobbled streets, boutiques, cafes and a lighthouse, with ocean sunsets from the ramparts.

destinations.name: Unawatuna
destinations.description: A sheltered golden bay with calm swimming, snorkelling and beach cafes, close to Galle.

destinations.name: Mirissa
destinations.description: A surf and sunset beach town and the best base for whale and dolphin watching trips, plus Coconut Tree Hill.

destinations.name: Trincomalee
destinations.description: A deep natural harbour on the east coast with quiet white-sand beaches at Uppuveli and Nilaveli, snorkelling, Koneswaram Temple and Pigeon Island.

faqs.question: How do I pay and is a deposit required?
faqs.answer: No online payment is taken at the moment. After you submit a booking request, the driver confirms the price and arrangements by WhatsApp or email. Payment is normally made in cash (LKR, USD, EUR or GBP) at the end of the service; a small deposit may be requested for longer tours.

faqs.question: What is your cancellation policy?
faqs.answer: Airport transfers can be cancelled free of charge up to 24 hours before pickup. Multi-day tours can be cancelled free up to 7 days before the start date. Please contact us as early as possible if your plans change.

faqs.question: Do you provide child seats?
faqs.answer: Yes, child and booster seats are available on request at no extra charge. Please mention the child's age in your booking notes so we can bring the right seat.

faqs.question: How much luggage can the vehicle carry?
faqs.answer: The Toyota Prius fits about 2 large suitcases plus small bags, and the KDH van about 8 large suitcases. If you travel with surfboards, golf clubs or other large items, tell us so we can recommend the right vehicle.

faqs.question: What if my flight is delayed?
faqs.answer: Your driver tracks your flight number and adjusts the pickup time automatically. There is no extra charge for delays, and 60 minutes of waiting time after landing is included.

faqs.question: Is it safe to travel by road in Sri Lanka?
faqs.answer: Roads can be busy and winding, so an experienced local driver makes a big difference. Vehicles are regularly serviced, insured and licensed, and the driver never rushes or drives tired.

faqs.question: Can I change the itinerary during the trip?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Our private tours are flexible; you can add stops, stay longer somewhere you love or skip something. Large changes may affect the final price and we will always tell you first.

faqs.question: Do you also help with hotels and tickets?
faqs.answer: We can recommend and help book hotels, safaris and train tickets. Entrance fees and accommodation are not included in the transport price unless the package says so.

regions.summary: Beach season runs December to April, with calm seas and sunny days. Southwest monsoon brings rain from May to September.
Hot and dry from May to September and good through February to April. Heavy rain in October to December.
Cool and misty year-round. Driest from January to March; March to May is ideal for Nuwara Eliya.
Opposite to the west coast: the east is best from April to September. Yala safaris are best from February to July.

info.title: ETA / Visa
info.body: Most visitors need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before arrival. Apply only through the official government website and carry a printed or digital approval together with your passport, valid for at least 6 months.

info.title: Currency
info.body: The Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR) is used everywhere. ATMs are widespread in towns, and cards are accepted in hotels and larger restaurants. Carry small notes for tuk-tuks, snacks and tips.

info.title: SIM Cards & Internet
info.body: Tourist SIM cards are sold at the airport arrivals hall with data packages from major operators. Coverage is good in towns and tourist areas but patchy in national parks and high hills.

info.title: Cultural Etiquette
info.body: Dress modestly at temples: cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes and hats. Never pose with your back to a Buddha statue, ask before photographing people, and use your right hand when giving or receiving.
